text: In the green heart of Fogny, where freshwater streams feed emerald rice valleys, lived Koochi Barama.
Koochi possessed a tongue so smooth that people said he could convince a fish that drowning was a blessing.
If he forgot to tie the family goats, he claimed a golden leopard had frightened them away.
If he spilled a calabash of palm oil, he swore an invisible wind from the clouds had tipped it over.
'Words are like smoke,' Koochi laughed to his companions.
'They dance in the air, and then they disappear.
Who could ever be hurt by smoke?'
